Why, then, must he still insist on knowing how deep or shallow her feeling is? I wish to know it, yet she deliberately will not let me know it; and so I desire all the more to know it. paragraphs.source_en: Note: The countless stars in the heavens are easy to measure, but the heart of that beauty is hard to fathom; yet once one has grown used to holding her tender body, one knows its weight and lightness. Why, then, must he still insist on knowing how deep or shallow her feeling is? I wish to know it, yet she deliberately will not let me know it; and so I desire all the more to know it. To speak in this way is truly to see through the hidden thoughts of foolish young lovers. This poem may be called a marvelous piece, and Gyatso a delightfully forthright man.
